'''Justise Winslow''' (born March 26, 1996) is an American [[basketball]] player who played at [[Duke University]]. He played [[small forward]] for the [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Blue Devils]].

Winslow was selected as a [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald’s All-American]] in 2014.<ref name=PafMAAG>{{cite web|url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/eye-on-college-basketball/24424133/players-announced-for-mcdonalds-all-american-game|title=Players announced for McDonald's All-American Game|accessdate=November 20, 2014|date=January 1, 2013|author=Borzello, Jeff|publisher=[[CBS Sports]]}}</ref>


==High School career==
Winslow was a four year starter at St.Johns High School in Houston, Texas. He started his career at St. John's with a league championship and went out in the same fashion. The reigning Gatorade Texas Player of the Year averaged 27.5 points, 13.6 rebounds, 3.5 assists, 2.1 blocks and 1.8 steals per game his Senior season for the Mavericks, who beat Kinkaid for the program's third SPC Division I crown in four years.

==College career==
Winslow averaged 14 points and five rebounds in his first five games in a Duke uniform.  Duke coach [[Mike Krzyzewski]] has compared Winslow's game to that of former Duke stars [[Tommy Amaker]] and [[Grant Hill]].<ref name=surprise>{{cite web|url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/eye-on-college-basketball/24833646/surprisingly-its-justise-winslow-not-okafor-whos-been-dukes-best-frosh|title=Surprisingly, it's Justise Winslow, not Okafor, who's been Duke's best frosh|accessdate=November 24, 2014|date=November 23, 2014|author=Norlander, Matt|publisher=[[CBS Sports]]}}</ref> On February 9, 2015, Winslow was named ACC Freshman of the Week.<ref name=ACCPOW11>{{cite web|title=ACC Basketball: Players of the Week Announced|url=http://www.theacc.com/news/acc-basketball-players-of-the-week-announced-02-09-2015|website=theACC.com|accessdate=19 May 2015|date=9 February 2015}}</ref> He was named an honorable mention All-ACC performer.<ref>{{cite web|title=ACSMA 2015 All-ACC Basketball Teams Announced|url=http://www.theacc.com/news/acsma-all-acc-basketball-teams-announced-03-08-2015|accessdate=April 29, 2015|work=[[Atlantic Coast Conference]]|date=March 8, 2015}}</ref> In the NCAA tournament, Winslow averaged 14.3 points and 9.3 rebounds per game en route to a national championship. He declared for the NBA Draft following the season, forgoing his final three years of collegiate eligibility. He is expected to be a top 5 pick.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Keeley|first1=Laure|title=Duke’s Justise Winslow to enter NBA Draft|url=http://www.newsobserver.com/sports/college/acc/duke/article18521150.html|accessdate=April 25, 2015|work=[[The News-Observer]]|date=April 14, 2015}}</ref>

==Personal==
His father, [[Rickie Winslow]], was a 6'8" forward for the [[University of Houston]] [[Houston Cougars men's basketball | Cougars basketball team]] from 1983-87, where he was a member of the famed [[Phi Slama Jama]] team that included [[Hakeem Olajuwon]] and [[Clyde Drexler]], and was selected 28th overall by the [[Chicago Bulls]] in the [[1987 NBA Draft]]. 

His mother, Robin Davis, is based in Houston.

Winslow's older brother Brandon owns a marketing company and is based in Los Angeles. His brother Josh is on the [[Dartmouth Big Green football | football team]] at [[Dartmouth College]], and his sister [[Houston Cougars women's basketball#2013.E2.80.9314 Roster|Bianca]], is on the basketball team at the [[Houston Cougars women's basketball | University of Houston]]. Half-brother Cedric lives in Houston.
